quizzes.title: India's Partnerships: Vietnam, NZ and SAARC
quizzes.passage:
India and Vietnam have raised their bilateral ties to an enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, a formal upgrade that followed a state visit by a Vietnamese leader. The two countries have also agreed on a trade goal and plan deeper defence cooperation, including joint development of advanced defence platforms, which is set out in a Joint Vision Statement. Vietnam has formally joined an Indo-Pacific initiative that India supports, and the relationship is linked to India's wider engagement with Southeast Asia.

India has also signed a free trade agreement with New Zealand. A free trade agreement is a pact between countries to reduce or eliminate customs duties and liberalise trade in services, and it also ensures investment protection and safeguards for intellectual property rights. Sensitive sectors such as dairy and agriculture are kept outside the deal to protect domestic producers, and the two countries have agreed to mutually recognise organic certification standards.

In South Asia, the SAARC currency swap framework is a bilateral arrangement between central banks. Members exchange domestic currencies at a predetermined rate and reverse the exchange at a future date. The framework provides short-term liquidity support to member nations, helps them during balance of payments crises, reduces dependence on external borrowing and strengthens regional financial stability.

questions.q: In which year did the RBI launch the SAARC currency swap framework?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the SAARC currency swap framework was launched by the RBI in 2012.

questions.q: What amount of defence line of credit has India extended to Vietnam?
questions.explanation: India has extended a USD 500 million defence line of credit to Vietnam.

questions.q: What bilateral trade target have India and Vietnam set for 2030?
questions.explanation: Both countries set a target of USD 25 billion in bilateral trade by 2030.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Indian exports to New Zealand face zero duty under the India-New Zealand FTA.
Reason (R): India gives New Zealand access to 100% of its tariff lines.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Indian exports do get full duty elimination, but India opens only 70.03% of its tariff lines, so R is false.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Sahyog   ->   A. ASI restoration of a site linked to the Champa civilisation
II. VINBAX   ->   B. Coast Guard exercise
III. My Son Sanctuary   ->   C. Pact to reduce dependence on critical mineral supply chains
IV. Strategic Rare Earths Pact   ->   D. Army exercise
questions.explanation: Sahyog is a Coast Guard exercise, VINBAX is an Army exercise, My Son is linked to ASI restoration, and the rare earths pact targets critical mineral supply chains.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Vietnam has formally joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.
II. New Zealand has committed to invest USD 20 billion over 15 years.
III. The SAARC currency swap tenure can be extended up to five times.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the SAARC swap tenure is extendable only twice.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The SAARC currency swap tenure is three months.
II. The Joint Vision Statement seeks reduced defence cooperation between India and Vietnam.
III. My Son Sanctuary is associated with the ancient Champa civilisation.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the Joint Vision Statement seeks deeper, not reduced, defence cooperation.

quizzes.title: India's Partnerships: Vietnam, NZ and SAARC
quizzes.passage:
India and Vietnam have agreed to lift their relationship to a higher strategic level after a state visit by a Vietnamese leader. The two countries have set a trade target for 2030 and plan closer defence ties, including work on advanced defence platforms. Vietnam has also formally joined an Indo-Pacific initiative that India promotes. Military exercises between the two countries also take place.

India has signed a free trade agreement with New Zealand. Such an agreement is a pact between countries that reduces customs duties and liberalises trade, and it provides investment protection and safeguards for intellectual property. In this deal India keeps some sensitive sectors outside its concessions to protect domestic producers, while New Zealand has also made an investment commitment. New Zealand is also a major trading partner for India in Oceania.

The SAARC currency swap framework is a bilateral arrangement between central banks. Members exchange domestic currencies at a predetermined rate and reverse the exchange later, which gives short-term liquidity support. The arrangement also aims to reduce dependence on external borrowing, promote the use of the Indian rupee internationally and strengthen regional financial stability. Such a framework is designed to help member nations in times of short-term financial need.

questions.q: Which Vietnamese leader's state visit preceded the upgrade of India-Vietnam ties? (Give the name.)
questions.explanation: The upgrade to an enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership followed the state visit of To Lam.

questions.q: What is the bilateral trade target for 2030, in USD billion?
questions.explanation: India and Vietnam set a target of USD 25 billion in bilateral trade by 2030.

questions.q: What defence line of credit did India extend to Vietnam, in USD million?
questions.explanation: India extended a USD 500 million defence line of credit to Vietnam.

questions.q: What percentage of Indian exports to New Zealand have their duties eliminated under the FTA? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The India-New Zealand FTA eliminates 100% of duties on Indian exports to New Zealand.

questions.q: What percentage of tariff lines does India keep under exclusion in the New Zealand FTA? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: India gives access to 70.03% of its tariff lines and keeps 29.97% under exclusion.

questions.q: Over how many years will New Zealand invest USD 20 billion? (in years)
questions.explanation: New Zealand plans to invest USD 20 billion over 15 years.

questions.q: What is the initial tenure of the SAARC currency swap, in months?
questions.explanation: The SAARC swap tenure is 3 months, extendable twice.

quizzes.title: Thucydides Trap, Ebola and Ecocide
quizzes.passage:
The Thucydides Trap is a phrase used in international relations to describe the danger of conflict when a rising power challenges a power that is already dominant. The idea comes from the writings of Thucydides, who analysed a long war between two rival powers. Its core idea is that fear and rivalry between powers can make a clash more likely, and the concept is often discussed in relation to a rising power and an existing global power. Critics argue that the idea oversimplifies politics by suggesting conflict is unavoidable, while others stress that diplomacy and economic links can prevent escalation.

The World Health Organization has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo to be a serious international health emergency. Under the International Health Regulations, such a declaration applies when a health risk could spread across borders and needs a coordinated response. Ebola is a severe viral disease that can affect humans and primates.

Ecocide refers to unlawful or reckless acts that cause severe, widespread or long-term environmental damage, carried out with knowledge that such damage is likely. The idea has gained legal attention, and several countries have written it into their own laws, which is one reason it is discussed in environmental debates.

questions.q: Which war did Thucydides analyse when developing the concept?
questions.explanation: Thucydides analysed the Peloponnesian War, fought between Athens and Sparta.

questions.q: Which strain of Ebola is linked to the WHO-declared outbreak in the DR Congo?
questions.explanation: The DR Congo outbreak is linked to the Bundibugyo strain.

questions.q: In which region of DR Congo is the Bundibugyo-linked outbreak located?
questions.explanation: The outbreak is located in the Ituri region of DR Congo.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Ebola is classified as a zoonotic disease.
Reason (R): Ebola was first identified in 1976.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the 1976 identification does not explain why Ebola is zoonotic.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Athens   ->   A. Dominant established power in the Thucydides account
II. Sparta   ->   B. Emerging power in the Thucydides account
III. Yambuku   ->   C. South Sudan site of a 1976 Ebola outbreak
IV. Nzara   ->   D. DR Congo site of a 1976 Ebola outbreak near the Ebola River
questions.explanation: Athens is the emerging power, Sparta the dominant established power, Yambuku the DR Congo site and Nzara the South Sudan site.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Thucydides argued that the growth of Athenian power and the fear it caused in Sparta made conflict increasingly inevitable.
II. Ebola belongs to the Filoviridae family.
III. Ecocide is recognised as a crime under the Rome Statute.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while ecocide is not currently recognised under the Rome Statute.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Rome Statute recognises four international crimes.
II. India has signed the Rome Statute.
III. Vietnam was the first country to codify ecocide.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while India has not signed the Rome Statute.

quizzes.title: Thucydides Trap, Ebola and Ecocide
quizzes.passage:
A rising power that challenges an established power can end up in conflict, a pattern that a historian's account of an old war helped to describe. Modern analysts apply this idea to today's great-power rivalries, though critics stress that it can make war seem more inevitable than it is. Diplomacy, trade ties and international institutions are often cited as ways to reduce the risk of confrontation.

Health authorities have also been busy. The World Health Organization has issued a formal emergency declaration over an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Such a declaration is used when a health risk could spread across borders and needs a coordinated global response. Ebola is a severe and fatal viral disease that can affect humans and primates. The disease was formerly known as Ebola haemorrhagic fever.

Environmental harm is drawing legal attention too. Acts that cause severe, widespread or long-term damage to nature, when committed knowingly or recklessly, are described as ecocide. Examples often cited include the Deepwater Horizon oil spill and large-scale deforestation in the Amazon. Several countries have written this idea into their own laws.

questions.q: What is the name of the historian whose analysis of the Peloponnesian War inspired the Thucydides Trap concept?
questions.explanation: The concept is named after the historian Thucydides and his account of the Peloponnesian War.

questions.q: Which Ebola strain is linked to the DR Congo outbreak?
questions.explanation: The WHO-declared outbreak in DR Congo is linked to the Bundibugyo strain.

questions.q: In which year was Ebola first identified?
questions.explanation: Ebola was first identified in 1976 during two simultaneous outbreaks.

questions.q: Which 1976 Ebola outbreak site in DR Congo lies near the Ebola River?
questions.explanation: Yambuku in DR Congo is near the Ebola River, and the other 1976 outbreak was at Nzara.

questions.q: In which country is Nzara, the site of the other 1976 Ebola outbreak?
questions.explanation: Nzara, the second 1976 outbreak site, is in South Sudan.

questions.q: Under which treaty is ecocide not currently recognised as an international crime?
accept: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
questions.explanation: Ecocide is not currently recognised under the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court.

questions.q: Which country was the first to codify ecocide in its laws?
questions.explanation: Vietnam was the first country to codify ecocide among the countries that have done so.

quizzes.title: Citizenship, Privilege and Elections
quizzes.passage:
Citizenship and parliamentary conduct are both constitutional matters. The Centre has notified draft amendments to the Citizenship Rules that tighten the rules for applicants with links to certain neighbouring countries. Such applicants must declare the passports they hold or have held, and they must give full passport details for verification. The rules sit within the constitutional framework for citizenship, which is a subject placed on the Union List.

Members of Parliament have their own tools for raising concerns. A privilege notice is a formal way for a member to allege a breach of parliamentary privilege or contempt of the House. The notice is submitted under the rules of the House concerned, and the presiding officer then decides whether it can be discussed or sent to a committee. The aim is to protect the dignity and independence of Parliament.

Elections in India follow a code issued by the Election Commission. The code is a set of guidelines and not a law, and it applies to political parties, candidates and the government in power. Its purpose is to ensure a free and fair contest. The Supreme Court has also introduced digital tools, including an online chatbot on its website that helps litigants find procedural information.

questions.q: Which Articles of the Constitution cover citizenship?
questions.explanation: The booklet places citizenship under Part II of the Constitution, Articles 5 to 11.

questions.q: What is the name of the AI-enabled chatbot integrated with the Supreme Court website?
questions.explanation: Su Sahay is an AI-enabled chatbot integrated with the Supreme Court website.

questions.q: How many modes of acquisition of citizenship does the Citizenship Act, 1955 list?
questions.explanation: The Act lists birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India does not permit dual citizenship.
Reason (R): Acquiring foreign citizenship leads to automatic termination of Indian citizenship.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Automatic termination of Indian citizenship on acquiring foreign citizenship is the reason India does not allow dual citizenship.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 105   ->   A. Procedure for submitting a privilege notice in Lok Sabha
II. Lok Sabha Rule 222   ->   B. Freedom of speech and immunity for legislative actions in Parliament
III. Harbans Singh Jalal case   ->   C. Article 324 described as a reservoir of power for the ECI
IV. Mohinder Singh Gill case   ->   D. MCC starts from the date of the election schedule announcement
questions.explanation: Article 105 gives freedom of speech, Rule 222 governs the Lok Sabha privilege notice, the Harbans Singh Jalal case fixes the start of the MCC, and the Mohinder Singh Gill case calls Article 324 a reservoir of power.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Electronic OCI cards have been introduced alongside physical OCI cards.
II. Under the draft rules, a foreign passport must be surrendered within 15 days of citizenship being granted.
III. The Rajya Sabha privilege notice is submitted under Rule 222.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the Rajya Sabha privilege notice is submitted under Rule 187, not Rule 222.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Lok Sabha Privileges Committee has 15 members nominated by the Speaker.
II. The Rajya Sabha Privileges Committee is chaired by the Chairman.
III. The Rajya Sabha Privileges Committee has 10 members.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the Rajya Sabha committee is chaired by the Deputy Chairman.

quizzes.title: Citizenship, Privilege and Elections
quizzes.passage:
Citizenship is a subject that the Constitution places under the Union, and the Citizenship Act sets out how citizenship can be acquired and lost. Under the latest draft changes, applicants who have held passports from certain neighbouring countries must declare them, and a foreign passport must be surrendered within a set period after citizenship is granted. Applicants must also provide full passport details so that the authorities can verify them.

Parliament also guards its own dignity. A member who believes a minister or an outside body has breached parliamentary privilege can raise the matter through a formal privilege notice, a mechanism that is grounded in the Constitution. Such a notice can be raised against a minister, a member or an outside individual or institution. The presiding officer then decides whether the House should discuss the matter or refer it to a privileges committee. The aim is to protect the authority and independence of Parliament.

Public life has its own rules during elections. The Election Commission issues guidelines so that contests are free and fair, and these guidelines stop the ruling party from gaining an unfair advantage. Meanwhile the Supreme Court is bringing case records from several levels of courts into one digital platform, called One Case One Data.

questions.q: In which year was the Citizenship Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Citizenship Act, 1955 sets out the modes of acquiring citizenship.

questions.q: How many days are allowed to surrender a foreign passport after citizenship is granted under the draft rules? (in days)
questions.explanation: Under the draft rules, a foreign passport must be surrendered within 15 days of citizenship being granted.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution is the privilege notice derived?
questions.explanation: The privilege notice is derived from Article 105 of the Constitution.

questions.q: Under which Rule of the Lok Sabha is a privilege notice submitted?
questions.explanation: A privilege notice is submitted under Lok Sabha Rule 222.

questions.q: Under which Rule of the Rajya Sabha is a privilege notice submitted?
questions.explanation: A privilege notice is submitted under Rajya Sabha Rule 187.

questions.q: Which 1978 case described Article 324 as a 'reservoir of power' for the Election Commission?
accept: Mohinder Singh Gill vs Chief Election Commissioner
questions.explanation: The 1978 judgment in Mohinder Singh Gill vs Chief Election Commissioner called Article 324 a reservoir of power.

questions.q: In which year was the Harbans Singh Jalal case decided?
questions.explanation: The Harbans Singh Jalal vs Union of India case, decided in 1997, held that the MCC starts from the date of the election schedule announcement.
